Log-Likelihood Components of an N-Mixture Model

Source: R/nmix.R
nmix_loglik.Rd

Computes, for every posterior draw, the site-level marginal log-likelihood and the observation (visit)-level log-likelihood of a binomial N-mixture model $$N_i \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_i), \quad y_{ij} \mid N_i \sim \mathrm{Binomial}(N_i, p_{ij}),$$ for sites \(i = 1, \ldots, I\) and visits \(j = 1, \ldots, J\). These are the inputs of ijk_nmix() and the two-stage bootstrap ijk_bootstrap_2stage().

Usage

nmix_loglik(y, lambda, p, N = NULL, Nmax_extra = 100)

Arguments

y

Numeric counts with \(I\) rows (sites) and \(J\) columns (visits); a numeric vector is treated as a one-column matrix. Counts must be finite non-negative integers, except that NA marks a missing visit. Every site must have at least one observed visit.

lambda

Finite positive numeric matrix (\(S \times I\)) of posterior draws of \(\lambda_i\); at least one draw is required.

p

Posterior draws of \(p_{ij}\): either an array (\(S \times I \times J\)) or a matrix (\(S \times IJ\)) whose columns are ordered as \(k = i + (j - 1) I\) (the column-major order used by JAGS for p[i,j]). Values for observed visits must be finite and between 0 and 1; values for missing visits are not used.

N

Optional numeric matrix (\(S \times I\)) of finite non-negative integer posterior draws of \(N_i\); each draw must be at least the largest observed count at its site. Required for obs_joint.

Nmax_extra

Non-negative integer; the summation grid for \(N_i\) extends Nmax_extra above \(\max_j y_{ij}\).

Value

An object of class "nmix_loglik" containing

site

\(S \times I\) matrix of site-level marginal log-likelihoods.

obs_rb

\(S \times IJ\) matrix (see Details). Missing visits are 0.

obs_joint

\(S \times IJ\) matrix or NULL.

condN

\(S \times I\) matrix of \(E[N_i \mid y_i, \theta]\).

obs_mask

Logical \(I \times J\) matrix, TRUE for observed visits.

tail_mass

Largest conditional probability at the upper end of the grid; a warning is issued when it exceeds 1e-8.

Details

The latent abundance \(N_i\) is summed out over the grid \(N = \max_j y_{ij}, \ldots, \max_j y_{ij} + \) Nmax_extra. Missing visits (NA in y) are dropped from the likelihood.

The observation-level log-likelihood is returned in two versions:

obs_rb

\(E[\log \mathrm{Bin}(y_{ij} \mid N, p_{ij}) \mid y_i, \theta]\), the expectation over the conditional posterior of \(N_i\). Use it for quantities that depend on the parameters only (e.g. regression coefficients, \(\lambda\)). It has smaller Monte Carlo noise.

obs_joint

\(\log \mathrm{Bin}(y_{ij} \mid N_i^{(s)}, p_{ij}^{(s)})\) evaluated at the posterior draws of \(N_i\). Use it for quantities that depend on the latent abundance (e.g. \(\sum_i N_i\)). Only available when N is supplied.

See also

nmix_draws(), ijk_nmix(), ijk_bootstrap_2stage()

Examples

set.seed(1)
I <- 10; J <- 3; S <- 50
y <- matrix(rpois(I * J, 3), I, J)
lambda <- matrix(rgamma(S * I, 20, 4), S, I)
p <- matrix(runif(S * I * J, 0.4, 0.7), S, I * J)
ll <- nmix_loglik(y, lambda, p)
dim(ll$site)
#> [1] 50 10
